html:
The Kalispel, also called the Pend d'Oreille, are an Indigenous people of the Northwest Plateau who speak an Interior Salish language. Their land followed the Flathead, Clark Fork and Pend Oreille rivers, from western Montana across northern Idaho to eastern Washington and into British Columbia. They called their home range Kaniksu.

They lived in many bands, probably eleven at first, in two main groups. The upstream people, the Upper Kalispel or Pend d'Oreille, also called the Camas People, now belong to the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes of the Flathead Reservation in Montana. The downstream people, the Lower Kalispel, now form the Kalispel Tribe of Indians in Washington.

They lived by fishing, hunting, and digging camas and other roots, moving with the seasons; upper bands crossed the mountains to hunt bison. French Canadian fur traders named them Pend d'Oreille, "hanging from the ear", for their shell earrings. Jesuit missionaries arrived in the 1840s. Their neighbours included the Flathead, the Spokane and the Nez Perce.
